Make bootstrap rows

Source: R/boot.R
trop_boot_rows.Rd

trop_boot_rows() makes the matrix of unit indices for the unit bootstrap of Algorithm 3. Each row of the matrix is one bootstrap draw. You can give the matrix to the argument boot_rows of trop() and trop_matrix(). When two or more fits use the same matrix, the draws have the same units. Then the fits have a joint bootstrap distribution. Use this for a test of many outcomes, for example with trop_stepdown().

Usage

trop_boot_rows(
  W,
  n_boot = 200L,
  strata = NULL,
  resample = c("stratified", "controls"),
  seed = NULL
)

Arguments

W

A matrix of treatment indicators with the values 0 and 1. Units are in rows.

n_boot

The number of bootstrap draws.

strata

An optional vector with one value for each unit. The values must not be NA.

resample

Use "stratified" or "controls". With "controls", the treated units do not change in a draw. Refer to the section Inference of trop().

seed

An optional integer seed. The function does not change the state of the random number generator in the R session.

Value

An integer matrix with n_boot rows and one column for each unit. Each value is a row number of W.

Details

A unit is a treated unit if its row of W has at least one value of 1. The function draws the treated units and the other units separately. With strata, it draws the units of each stratum separately. Thus, each draw has the same number of treated units and of other units in each stratum as the data.

A fit with fixed tuning parameters makes the same draws from the same seed. Cross-validation with cv_cells uses random numbers before the bootstrap. Then the draws are different.

A fit uses a treated unit only if the unit has a treated cell with an outcome. If all treated cells of a unit have an NA outcome, the fit draws the unit with the other units. Use W with such units set to 0 to get the same draws.

See also

trop_effects(), trop_stepdown()

Examples

W <- matrix(0L, 8, 5)
W[1:3, 4:5] <- 1L
trop_boot_rows(W, n_boot = 3, seed = 1)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8]
#> [1,]    1    3    1    5    8    6    5    6
#> [2,]    3    1    1    8    5    5    4    8
#> [3,]    1    1    1    8    8    5    5    4
trop_boot_rows(W, n_boot = 3, strata = rep(c("a", "b"), 4), seed = 1)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3] [,4] [,5] [,6] [,7] [,8]
#> [1,]    1    3    2    5    7    4    8    8
#> [2,]    3    3    2    5    5    4    4    6
#> [3,]    3    3    2    5    5    8    4    4
